title: trust: aggregate every direct parent; never select relationship_parents[0]
description:
## Problem
The original CLIPS model stores an arbitrary set of masters (`ioc.trusts`): malicious propagation fires from any malicious master, while benign propagation fires only when the child has at least one master and no non-BENIGN master (~/src_fast/ioc.clp:85-99).

The connector reads every marked outgoing relationship but discards all except `relationship_parents[0]` (connectors/ioc-trust-cluster/src/connector.py:1203-1208). OpenCTI does not promise a stable order. A benign first parent can therefore attach `fp-candidate` despite another direct malicious parent; a later parent can also be silently ignored.

## Small fix
Classify all direct connector-owned parents together: malicious wins if any direct parent is malicious; benign only if one or more parents exist and all are confirmed benign; otherwise UNKNOWN. Keep direct one-hop fanout. Do not add a graph walker.

## Acceptance
- A child with one malicious and one benign parent receives only malicious-cascade.
- A child with an UNKNOWN and a benign parent receives neither inherited label.
- A child with only benign parents may receive fp-candidate.
- Relationship list order does not change the result.
- Focused regression tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented by hc7.1: all direct connector-owned parents are reduced together (malicious wins, benign only when all parents benign, otherwise UNKNOWN); order-independent regressions added; ioc-trust-cluster tests pass (219 passed).

title: B1 · PSL missing — ccTLD domains get wrong parent (`bbc.co.uk` → `co.uk`)
description:
Migrated from TODO.md.

Old ID: B1
Connector: trust
Priority: P0
Batch: —

---

`_extract_parent("Domain-Name")` takes the last two labels unconditionally:

```python
parts = value.rstrip(".").split(".")
if len(parts) > 2:
    return ("Domain-Name", ".".join(parts[-2:]))
```

For `cdn.bbc.co.uk` this returns `co.uk` — a TLD registry, not a registrant.
Every `.co.uk` domain clusters under the same parent, enabling cross-tenant
malicious-cascade. Same problem applies to `com.au`, `co.jp`, `org.uk`, etc.

The NS cycle guard in `_get_authoritative_ns` has the same flaw: it checks
`ns.split(".")[-2:] == domain`, which fails to detect the cycle for
`domain="example.co.uk"` and `ns="ns1.example.co.uk"` (`co.uk != example.co.uk`).

**Dependency:** Fix before #2 (NS Allowlist uses same two-label extraction)
and before #1 (Parent Aggregator needs correct domain parents).

**Fix:** Add `tldextract` (or `publicsuffix2`) to `requirements.txt` and
replace the slice with a PSL-aware registrable-domain extraction.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `cdn.bbc.co.uk` → parent `bbc.co.uk`
- [ ] `mail.example.com.au` → parent `example.com.au`
- [ ] `sub.evil.com` → parent `evil.com` (no regression on simple TLDs)
- [ ] NS cycle guard updated and tested with multi-part TLD domain + self-referential NS

title: B3 · X509 parent search always misses → duplicate CA anchors every run
description:
Migrated from TODO.md.

Old ID: B3
Connector: trust
Priority: P0
Batch: —

---

`_find_or_create_parent("X509-Certificate", issuer_dn)` searches via
`_find_observable`, which always includes `{"key": "value", "values": [issuer_dn]}`
as a base filter. OpenCTI X509-Certificate observables have no `value` field;
their identity is a fingerprint hash. The `AND` filter always returns zero
results, so `create` is called on every enrichment run of every child cert.
Each run produces a new duplicate CA anchor observable.

**Fix:** Remove the `value` base filter for X509; search by `subject` alone:

```python
if obs_type == "X509-Certificate":
    results = self.helper.api.stix_cyber_observable.list(
        types=["X509-Certificate"],
        filters={"mode": "and",
                 "filters": [{"key": "subject", "values": [value]}],
                 "filterGroups": []},
        first=1,
    )
    existing = results[0] if results else None
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Second enrichment run of a cert issued by the same CA finds the existing
      anchor and does not call `create`
- [ ] Test: call `process_message` twice for the same leaf cert; `create` called
      exactly once across both runs

title: trust: retract connector-owned cascade labels when current parents no longer support them
description:
## Problem
The connector says OpenCTI cannot remove labels and only creates an advisory note when a parent ceases to be malicious (src/connector.py:964-985, :1150-1159). After the multi-parent truth table is implemented, use reserved connector-owned labels only and remove an inherited label when no current direct connector-owned parent supports it. Never remove an analyst/feed label. Keep an audit note for the state transition.

- A child loses malicious-cascade when no direct parent is confirmed malicious.
- A child loses inherited fp-candidate when no direct parent is confirmed benign, without removing an independently sourced FP label.

title: trust: make NS hierarchy opt-in and stop creating synthetic X509 CA observables
description:
## Problem
The auto connector is enabled for every domain and certificate. Defaults enable DNS NS lookup (src/connector.py:175-179) and an empty allowlist means every provider is accepted (:191-198, :539-554). A single DNS NS is not an ownership/trust relationship and can form very large cross-tenant clusters; the existing allowlist cannot be complete.

For certificates, issuer DN is also not a unique CA certificate identity. The connector creates a synthetic X509 observable with only `subject` (:821-831) and later merges all certificates sharing that DN (:698-706). This conflates distinct CA certificates/rotations and is not an observed IOC.

## Ponytail recommendation
Keep deterministic registered-domain and ASN/RDAP CIDR relationships. Make NS discovery opt-in (default false) and do not create synthetic X509 anchors. Only link an X509 parent when a stable issuer-certificate identity is already supplied by the input; otherwise skip it.

## Acceptance
- Default deployment makes no DNS NS request and creates no NS relationship.
- No X509 observable is created solely from an issuer DN/subject.
- Existing deterministic domain/CIDR behavior remains covered.
- README describes the narrower, evidence-backed default.
close_reason: Completed 1qc series: NS discovery is opt-in and synthetic X509 CA anchors are no longer created/merged; README documents narrower defaults. ioc-trust-cluster tests pass (225 passed).

title: ponytail: remove automatic parent score promotion from the first trust-chain release
description:
## Bloat / risk
~/src_fast/ioc.clp has no child-to-parent reputation promotion: it only creates edges and propagates existing MALICIOUS/BENIGN verdicts downward. The connector added a second inference system (src/connector.py:1039-1094) that treats any non-cascaded score as direct evidence, writes score 80 or 15 to a structural anchor, then fans that inferred score back to siblings.

There is no source/provenance field proving a score is direct, no baseline score to restore, and no safe demotion path. This creates irreversible, self-amplifying reputation changes outside the original model.

## Ponytail decision
Delete parent promotion and its `PROMOTER_*` configuration from the first deploy. Structural edges plus downward labels are sufficient to prove whether the connector is useful. Reintroduce aggregation only with a concrete evidence/provenance model and a demonstrated operational need.

## Acceptance
- No connector path writes a parent score from child scores.
- `PROMOTER_*`, promotion notes, and promotion-specific tests are removed.
- Parent-triggered direct fanout remains.
- Full connector tests pass.
close_reason: Removed automatic parent score promotion from first trust-chain release; no connector path writes parent score from child scores, and promotion config/notes/tests are gone. Tests pass (220 passed).

title: trust: paginate relationship fanout and sightings instead of silently capping at 100
description:
## Problem
pycti 6.6.18 defaults `stix_core_relationship.list()` and `stix_sighting_relationship.list()` to `first=100`, `getAll=False` (installed client sources). The connector passes neither at src/connector.py:742-745, :773-776, :880-883, or :918. Thus a parent with >100 children is promoted and fanned out from an arbitrary prefix, and a child with >100 sightings can be undercounted after source filtering. The code comment at :916 incorrectly says it fetches all sightings.

This makes the declared percentage thresholds and one-hop cascade depend on pagination, not data.

## Small fix
Use pycti pagination (`getAll=True`) for connector-owned relationship evaluation and for sightings where an exact count is required. If an explicit bounded strategy is chosen for very large clusters, document that it is approximate and do not use it for promotion.

## Acceptance
- A mocked two-page relationship result is fully considered for fanout and promotion.
- A sighting-source-filter case where qualifying sightings occur after the first 100 is counted correctly.
- No API call relies on pycti's implicit `first=100` default.
close_reason: Fixed silent first-100 cap for trust-edge reads and sightings by using pycti pagination; regression coverage added. Tests pass (223 passed).

title: V6 · Poll `raise_for_status()` leaks `HTTPError` past `VectraMetadataError` → kills whole cycle
description:

```python

    pd: dict = poll.json()
except ValueError:
    poll.raise_for_status()   # ← raises requests.HTTPError on 5xx — not wrapped
    raise VectraMetadataError(...)
```

When the poll response is a 5xx with a non-JSON body (nginx error page),
`poll.json()` raises `ValueError`. `poll.raise_for_status()` then raises
`requests.HTTPError`, which is NOT caught by the `except requests.RequestException`
above (that wraps only the `requests.get()` call).

`HTTPError` propagates past `_process_query`'s `except VectraMetadataError`
and aborts the entire cycle — not just the one failing query.

**Fix:**
```python
except ValueError:
    try:
        poll.raise_for_status()
    except requests.RequestException as http_exc:
        raise VectraMetadataError(
            f"Poll HTTP {poll.status_code}: {http_exc}"
        ) from http_exc
    raise VectraMetadataError(
        f"Poll returned non-JSON HTTP {poll.status_code}"
    )
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] 5xx non-JSON poll response raises `VectraMetadataError`, not `HTTPError`
- [ ] `_process_query` catches it; remaining queries continue

title: Enrich existing OpenCTI observables with targeted Vectra popularity evidence
description:
Extend connector-vectra-metadata-fp to annotate existing OpenCTI observables with time-bounded popularity evidence from Vectra Metadata so analysts do not need an ad hoc Metadata lookup during every detection investigation.

One tenant is sufficient. Evidence is keyed by the Observable and a configured opaque source/tenant identifier so additional tenants can strengthen confidence without changing the model. Store aggregates only; never raw users, internal hosts, events, or customer identities.

Start with types proven in the current snapshot:
- Domain-Name: candidate-targeted DNS query, TLS SNI, and HTTP Host breadth.
- IPv4-Addr: candidate-targeted shared successful M365 sign-in usage; add destination-session breadth only after its targeted query is validated.

The broad DNS/SNI GROUP BY queries can return a successful zero-row result on this Metadata service despite populated tables. Pull candidate values from OpenCTI and query them in bounded batches (50-100 values) using IN clauses, dt plus event-time filters, and per-value aggregation.

This is popularity context, not a whitelist. Do not create Indicators, lower scores, set fp-confirmed, or suppress detections. Default to updating existing observables only. X509 is deferred because Metadata exposes serial/subject/issuer but current detections expose no exact certificate identity or fingerprint; never create synthetic certificates from issuer/subject alone.
design:
Reuse the existing connector and OpenCTI observable APIs. For each candidate Observable, upsert connector-owned labels and one concise deterministic evidence Note per configured source/tenant (or a native Sighting if the real API proves it carries the required counts): opaque source ID, signal set, distinct host/user breadth, event count, first/last seen, lookback, and query version.

Neutral local labels:
- vectra-metadata:popular-domain
- vectra-metadata:shared-auth-ip
- vectra-metadata:popularity-conflict when malicious evidence coexists

A separate shadow rule may add herd-common-candidate only when multiple distinct sources agree. Keep VECTRA_FP_CREATE_MISSING=false for rollout. Bulk IPv4 creation is out of scope because it can trigger automatic enrichment calls.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Existing OpenCTI Domain-Name and IPv4-Addr values are read in bounded pages and queried in batches of at most 100.
2. Domain evidence combines exact normalized DNS query, SNI server_name, and HTTP host results; IPv4 evidence supports recurring successful M365 use by distinct users.
3. Queries use both dt and event-time filters and distinguish provider/query failure from a true zero match.
4. Reruns idempotently update one connector-owned evidence record per configured source/tenant and Observable instead of duplicating notes or labels.
5. Evidence contains only an opaque source ID and aggregate signal/count/time/breadth data; no raw internal identifiers are stored or shared.
6. Default mode creates no observables or indicators, changes no score, assigns no fp-confirmed state, and performs no detection suppression.
7. Existing malicious scores/labels remain authoritative and produce visible popularity-conflict context rather than a benign verdict.
8. Tests cover batching, normalization, source isolation, idempotency, zero-vs-error handling, stale evidence removal, and malicious/popular coexistence.
9. A shadow run reports candidate count and sampled evidence before labels are enabled; one tenant is sufficient to run it.

description:
Build privacy-safe Vectra popularity context for existing external IPv4 and domain Observables without creating a new graph platform.

One tenant is enough to produce useful local popularity evidence. Additional tenants increase confidence and can support a stronger herd-common-candidate signal, but they are not an implementation prerequisite. Reuse the OpenCTI Observable as the shared node and attach aggregate-only evidence; never export raw users, internal hosts, events, or customer identities.
design:
Use existing platform features only:
- Existing IPv4/domain Observables are the common entities.
- Targeted Metadata queries and idempotent evidence writes live in open-cti-y5g.
- Store one native evidence record per source/tenant and Observable with only an opaque source ID, signal names, first/last seen, recurrence, and breadth buckets.
- One source may add only neutral local popularity context; multiple sources may additionally qualify for herd-common-candidate.
- Reuse ioc-trust-cluster for root-domain/CIDR/ASN relationships.
- Popularity never sets fp-confirmed, lowers scores, creates Indicators, or suppresses detections.

No custom tenant/signal nodes, central scoring service, service-anchor taxonomy, or certificate graph.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A privacy-safe replay over each available tenant reports useful local evidence and, when multiple tenants are available, overlap and malicious-conflict rates; lack of a second tenant does not block implementation.
2. open-cti-y5g performs bounded candidate-targeted queries and idempotently stores aggregate-only evidence per source/tenant and Observable.
3. Single-source evidence produces only neutral local popularity context.
4. A shadow-only herd-common-candidate rule requires multiple distinct sources and strong evidence, blocks on malicious contradictions, and remains analyst-reviewed.

title: Patch IPQS connector to surface insufficient-credit failures as work errors
description:
## Problem

When the IPQS connector receives an 'insufficient credits' response from the provider, it logs the error but allows the OpenCTI work record to complete with `status=complete, errors=[]`. Callers (including opencti-ioc) cannot distinguish a genuine no-hit (IPQS found nothing) from a provider failure (IPQS was never actually queried). This produces silent false-negatives in enrichment coverage.

Observed during 2026-10-08 investigation: 15 supported IOCs returned unexplained unknown/miss in opencti-ioc output. Connector logs showed every query failed with 'You have insufficient credits to make this query'. Work records showed complete/no-errors for all 15.

## Root Cause

The upstream IPQS connector swallows the credit-failure response rather than calling `self.helper.connector_logger.error()` or raising to mark the work item failed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. IPQS insufficient-credit (and auth failure) responses result in `work.errors` being populated — the work record must NOT complete cleanly on a provider failure.
2. opencti-ioc (and any caller inspecting work records) can distinguish provider-unavailable from a legitimate no-hit.
3. Patch is applied via `cidr-enrichment-filter/patch.py` alongside the existing CIDR-skip patches, or via a dedicated connector override layer.
4. Tests cover: (a) credit-failure response → work error populated, (b) legitimate no-hit → work completes cleanly.

## Notes

The auto-enrichment backlog (soc-zyqf / CONNECTOR_AUTO=true) is already fixed. This issue tracks the orthogonal error-propagation gap that remains even for manual/GraphQL-requested enrichment.
Related: open-cti-4ma.3 tracks the broader quota circuit-break layer (deferred); this issue is narrower — just correct error propagation for the failure case that already exists.
Evidence: /tmp/ioc-compare-20261008/xtm-connector-ipqs-1.log, opencti-enrich-raw/opencti-work-*.json

## Labels
enrichment, error-propagation, ipqs, opencti, patch
close_reason: IPQS provider/auth failures now raise into OpenCTI work errors; neutral successful responses remain clean. Patch tested, image rebuilt, and connector redeployed.

title: Add RabbitMQ queue-depth monitoring and VT connector backlog recovery runbook
description:
## Problem

The VirusTotal connector uses a single RabbitMQ consumer. When the queue depth grows (observed: 17,110 ready + 1 unacknowledged during the Oct-2026 investigation), there is no alerting and no documented recovery path. Even with CONNECTOR_AUTO=false, a sustained burst of manual GraphQL enrichment requests against a quota-exhausted key could rebuild a queue that silently starves later jobs with no visible signal until the investigation SLO is already broken.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A queue-depth check (e.g. RabbitMQ management API or docker stats) is documented so on-call can assess connector health in under 60 seconds.
2. Thresholds are defined: warn at >50 ready jobs, page/escalate at >500 ready jobs or >1 unacknowledged job held for >5 minutes.
3. A documented, approval-gated backlog recovery procedure exists covering:
   - How to purge the VT listen queue safely (name pattern: listen_<connector-id>)
   - How to restart the connector without data loss for in-flight work
   - How to verify the queue drains and manual enrichment resumes
4. Procedure is tested in staging before merge.

## Notes

Observed queue name: listen_c12d2c3a-9036-4f7c-a05a-f3b75e0d5bde (connector-id-derived).
Evidence from soc-kwbw: /tmp/ioc-compare-20261008/rabbitmq-queues.txt.

title: Reuse known ASN-backed CIDRs before RDAP lookup
description:
IOC Trust Cluster currently caches RDAP results by exact IP. A newly seen IP therefore performs RDAP even when another IP already established the same CIDR anchor and CIDR→ASN ownership edge in OpenCTI.

Before RDAP, longest-prefix match the IP against existing connector-created, ASN-backed CIDR anchors. On a match, reuse that CIDR and its ASN relationship; call RDAP only on a miss. Do not match arbitrary feed-created CIDRs, which may be stale, overly broad, or have different semantics. Use the standard-library ipaddress module and a bounded in-memory index loaded once at startup and updated when this connector creates/discovers anchors.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Existing direct child→CIDR relationships remain the first lookup path and make no RDAP request.
2. A new IP inside an indexed connector-owned, ASN-backed CIDR reuses the most-specific matching CIDR without RDAP.
3. Overlapping anchors select the longest prefix.
4. Arbitrary CIDRs without the connector-owned ASN relationship/anchor provenance are ignored.
5. A miss performs the existing RDAP flow, exact OpenCTI reuse/create, and adds the resulting anchor to the local index.
6. IPv4 and IPv6 are covered; invalid, private, reserved, and CIDR-valued inputs preserve current behavior.
7. Tests prove two different IPs in one known prefix cause at most one RDAP discovery and reuse one CIDR/ASN chain.
notes: Implemented a bounded per-session longest-prefix index sourced only from connector-owned CIDR→ASN belongs-to edges. The index loads before queue listening, updates after successful new CIDR→ASN links, and falls back to existing RDAP behavior on misses/load failures. Added IPv4/IPv6, provenance filtering, longest-prefix, private-address, bound, and peer-IP reuse tests; updated connector documentation. Validation: 235 pytest tests pass, py_compile and git diff checks pass, Docker image builds, and the deployed connector loaded 100 trusted CIDR anchors before listening.
close_reason: Implemented, tested, and deployed trusted CIDR prefix reuse before RDAP

title: Stop repeated calls on quota exhaustion and expose enrichment usage
description:
Add a small quota guard around on-demand enrichment. Today IPQS continues calling the provider after receiving "insufficient credits" (342 rejected attempts were observed in 24 hours), while VirusTotal retries HTTP 429 responses. A failed quota response should stop further paid calls for a bounded cooldown and return a clear status to the requesting GraphQL work item.

Prefer provider response headers and existing connector metrics over a new quota service. Include duplicate-request protection only if OpenCTI has no native recent-enrichment guard.
acceptance_criteria:
1. IPQS insufficient-credit responses and VirusTotal 429/quota responses open a provider-specific circuit for a configurable bounded cooldown.
2. Requests received while open make zero provider API calls and complete with an actionable quota/cooldown message.
3. Metrics distinguish requested, executed, skipped, successful, failed, and quota-blocked enrichments by provider and observable type without logging secrets or observable values.
4. A documented reset/recovery path exists and normal GraphQL-requested enrichment resumes after recovery.
5. Tests cover opening, blocking, expiry/reset, and independent VT/IPQS circuit state.
notes: Deferred after 4ma review: CONNECTOR_AUTO=false removes the observed unbounded automatic traffic, so a custom circuit breaker and metrics layer are not justified yet. Revisit only if authorized GraphQL/UI users create measurable quota pressure, repeated provider-quota failures, or a requirement for hard per-user/provider budgets.

title: Reduce per-request VirusTotal/IPQS API cost

Audit the installed connector versions and make each user-requested enrichment use the fewest provider calls that still returns the required reputation result.

Remove misleading settings and explicitly select a low-cost lookup-only profile.

3. Optional VirusTotal YARA/relationship calls are disabled or justified with measured request counts.

title: Vectra FP: raw broad-reach IPs are weak whitelist context, not confirmed benign
description:
Broad-reach external IPs are useful for the Vectra metadata whitelist/cache, but they are the weakest benign signal. Public cloud/CDN/anycast IPs are shared, recycled, and can serve both benign and malicious content. A high-breadth IP is valuable popularity context for fast triage, not proof that every child URL/domain/use of that IP is benign.

Re-scoped goal: keep raw IP mining enabled so popular infrastructure clusters can be created, but distinguish raw broad-reach IPs from stronger benign signals. Domain-based queries (DNS/SNI/HTTP host/beacon domain) preserve application identity and are safer. M365 shared-auth IPs identify corporate egress/VPN/proxy infrastructure and are a stronger benign signal for that exact IP.

Ponytail path: do not skip Q1 and do not build a policy engine. Add one Q1-specific weak source label (for example `vectra-metadata-popular-ip`) and keep cascade-capable labels off by default. Retrieval can use that label as weak whitelist/cache context.

Acceptance criteria:
- Q1 `broad_reach_ips` still mines/creates popular IP observables by default.
- Q1 raw IPs are labelled as weak popularity context, not confirmed benign.
- Q1 raw IPs do not trigger trust-cluster benign cascade by default.
- Domains and M365 shared-auth IP behavior remains available as stronger benign context.
- Operators can opt into raw-IP-as-benign labeling if they accept shared-infra risk.

title: Vectra FP: create missing observables by default for whitelist/cache mining
description:
Re-scoped after review: the original default-off proposal is wrong for this connector. Vectra metadata mining is intended to proactively build a whitelist/cache of popular/known infrastructure for fast retrieval and triage. Creating missing observables is not bloat in that model; it is the product.

Current design:
- `VECTRA_FP_CREATE_MISSING` exists and defaults to `true` for whitelist/cache mining.
- Operators that want enrichment-only behavior can set `VECTRA_FP_CREATE_MISSING=false`.
- Missing-skips are counted in `_skipped_missing`; follow-up is only to expose that count in cycle logs.
- Signal-strength safety is handled separately: raw broad-reach IPs now use weak `vectra-metadata-popular-ip`; stronger domain/M365 signals use `vectra-metadata-benign`; cascade-capable labels are not default.

New acceptance:

- Keep enrichment-only opt-out documented by env var.
- Add/keep cycle summary visibility for skipped missing when opt-out is used.
- Do not remove proactive observable creation.

title: Vectra FP: SQL grouping splits breadth away from the IOC identity
description:
Several SQL templates group by context fields that are not the IOC identity:
- Q1 groups IPs by `resp_domain`, port, and service.
- Q4 groups HTTP hosts before Python strips `:port`.
- Q5 groups beacon rows by `resp_domains`, `resp_ip`, service, and beacon type.

This can under-count common IOCs and creates duplicate rows that are later dropped by `_seen_this_cycle`. If `1.2.3.4` is contacted by 30 hosts split across three ports/domains, no row may pass a host threshold of 10/20 even though the IP is clearly fleet-wide.

Ponytail path: group by the IOC value only in SQL, aggregate context with cheap counts/min/max/sample fields. Do not preserve exact per-port/per-service granularity unless an operator asks for it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Q1 breadth is counted per `id.resp_h`, not per `(ip, domain, port, service)`.
- HTTP host extraction/SQL handles `host:port` without splitting breadth by port.
- Beacon breadth is counted per emitted IOC value or post-query aggregation accounts for splits.
- Tests cover split rows that should still produce one high-breadth IOC.

title: Vectra FP: aggregate query signals before importing IOCs
description:
Current import path is per-query and first-match-wins:
- `_process_query()` imports immediately.
- `_seen_this_cycle` drops later hits for the same `(type, value)`.
- The note/context comes from whichever query ran first, not necessarily the strongest signal.

That loses the best evidence. Example: a domain seen in DNS and beacon keeps only DNS context; an IP split across query families may never show that multiple independent signals agree.

Ponytail path: keep the six SQL queries if needed, but aggregate in memory before touching OpenCTI. Key by `(ioc_type, value)`, keep max breadth + list of query names/context snippets, then import once.

Acceptance criteria:
- One OpenCTI lookup/create per IOC per cycle, not per query hit.
- Discovery note lists all query names that matched the IOC in that cycle.
- Optional safety gate can require `min_signals >= 2` for direct benign/cascade labels.
- Unit test covers duplicate IOC from two query definitions keeping both signals.

title: B16 · `fp_cascade_score_max` not validated — fp-candidate can reach malicious-scored observables
description:

**Priority: P2 — silent data quality corruption on misconfiguration**

The CONFIRMED_BENIGN cascade guard:

```python
if (
    score <= self.fp_cascade_score_max
    and LABEL_FP_CANDIDATE      not in labels
    and LABEL_MALICIOUS_CASCADE not in labels
    and not has_malicious
):
```

When `TRUST_CLUSTER_FP_CASCADE_SCORE_MAX >= TRUST_CLUSTER_MALICIOUS_SCORE_MIN`

also labelled benign.

The docstring already says "Must be kept below `TRUST_CLUSTER_MALICIOUS_SCORE_MIN`"

```python
if (
    score <= self.fp_cascade_score_max
    and score < self.malicious_score_min   # ← add this
    and LABEL_FP_CANDIDATE      not in labels
    and LABEL_MALICIOUS_CASCADE not in labels
    and not has_malicious
):
```

This closes the gap regardless of how operators configure the thresholds.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Child with score=75, `fp_cascade_score_max=80`, `malicious_score_min=70`

title: V17 · No threshold lower-bound: `host_threshold=0` marks everything fp-candidate
description:

**Priority: P2 — foot-gun with real data quality impact**

`VECTRA_FP_HOST_BREADTH_THRESHOLD` and `VECTRA_FP_USER_BREADTH_THRESHOLD`
default to 10 and 20.  No validation prevents setting them to 0 or 1.

With `VECTRA_FP_HOST_BREADTH_THRESHOLD=0`:
- Each query builds SQL with `HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT id.orig_h) >= 0`
- This condition is always true — every row in the table within the lookback
  window is returned (up to `max_results`)
- Up to 500 × 6 = 3,000 IPs and domains per cycle receive `fp-candidate`,
  regardless of whether they are actually broadly observed
- This could cascade into ioc-trust-cluster, marking CIDR parents as benign
  and suppressing malicious-cascade on their children

The same applies to `VECTRA_FP_USER_BREADTH_THRESHOLD=0` for Q6 (M365 auth IPs).

**Fix:** Validate at init; clamp with a warning or raise:

```python
if self.host_threshold < 2:
    raise ValueError(
        f"VECTRA_FP_HOST_BREADTH_THRESHOLD={self.host_threshold} is dangerously low; "
        "minimum is 2.  Default is 10."
    )
```

Or a softer approach: warn and clamp to a safe minimum.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `VECTRA_FP_HOST_BREADTH_THRESHOLD=0` raises `ValueError` (or logs `WARNING` and clamps)

title: B10 · IPv6 literal URL hosts: `.split(":")[0]` corrupts address; parent extraction silently drops
description:
Migrated from TODO.md.

Old ID: B10
Connector: trust
Priority: P3
Batch: —

---

`_extract_parent("Url")` does:

```python
host = (parsed.hostname or "").lower().split(":")[0]
```

For `http://[2001:db8::1]/path`, `parsed.hostname` returns `"2001:db8::1"`. The
`.split(":")[0]` then truncates it to `"2001"` — a single decimal number that
fails both the IPv4 regex and the domain validator. Parent extraction returns
`None` silently.

The `.split(":")[0]` was presumably intended to strip ports from `host:port`
strings, but `urlparse` already strips ports via `.hostname` (vs `.netloc`).
It is redundant for IPv4/domain URLs and actively wrong for IPv6.

**Fix:** Remove the `.split(":")[0]`, then add an IPv6 branch:

```python
host = (parsed.hostname or "").lower()   # urlparse already strips port
if not host:
    return None
try:
    ipaddress.IPv6Address(host)
    return self._extract_parent("IPv6-Addr", host)
except ValueError:
    pass
if re.match(r"^\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}$", host):
    return self._extract_parent("IPv4-Addr", host)
return self._extract_parent("Domain-Name", host)
```

title: V11 · OAuth2 token cache discarded on every cycle
description:
Migrated from TODO.md.

Old ID: V11
Connector: vectra
Priority: P3
Batch: —

---

`_build_client()` is called at the top of each loop iteration, creating a fresh
`VectraMetadataClient` instance. `_bearer_token` and `_token_expiry` start at
`None`/`0.0`, so a new OAuth2 token request fires every cycle.

For the default `interval_sec=86400`, one extra token per day is harmless. At
lower intervals (development, `interval_sec=300`), this hits OAuth2 rate limits.

The `ponytail:` comment in `_build_client` already acknowledges this. Filing
here so it is tracked.

`self._client` already exists on the instance (initialized to `None`). The fix
is straightforward: cache it, and reset to `None` only on `VectraMetadataError`
so a broken client is rebuilt automatically.

```python
def run(self) -> None:
    while True:
        if self._client is None:
            self._client = self._build_client()
        if self._client is not None:
            try:
                self._run_cycle(self._client)
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                raise
            except VectraMetadataError:
                self._client = None   # force rebuild next cycle
                self.helper.log_error(...)
            except Exception as exc:
                self.helper.log_error(...)
        time.sleep(self.interval_sec)
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] With `interval_sec=300`, token is fetched once and reused until near expiry
- [ ] `VectraMetadataError` during a cycle causes client rebuild on next cycle
- [ ] Non-auth cycle errors do not force a client rebuild

When `_find_observable` fails (transient 5xx, timeout), it returns `None`.
`_import_ioc` interprets `None` as "observable does not exist" and calls
`_create_observable`.  If the observable already exists in OpenCTI, this may
create a duplicate, depending on whether OpenCTI's `stix_cyber_observable.create`
is idempotent for the same (type, value) pair.

Even if OpenCTI deduplicates, the lookup failure is invisible at DEBUG —
consistent with B17/V12 pattern.

**Fix:** Change to `log_warning`.  Optionally propagate the exception so
`_import_ioc` can skip the observable rather than blindly creating.

```python

    if client is not None:

```

`_build_client` catches `VectraMetadataError` and returns `None`.  Any other
exception (e.g., a bug in env-var processing, an unexpected `OSError`) propagates
out of the `while True` loop and crashes the connector entirely rather than
logging and retrying on the next cycle.

In practice `_build_client` only reads env vars and constructs a `VectraMetadataClient`,
which raises only `VectraMetadataError`.  Risk is very low but the loop should
be defensive.

**Fix:** Wrap `_build_client` call in the same try-except:

```python
try:
    client = self._build_client()
except Exception as exc:
    self.helper.log_error(f"[vectra-fp] client init error: {exc}\n{traceback.format_exc()}")
    client = None
```

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Unexpected exception in `_build_client` logs at ERROR and sleeps for next cycle
- [ ] Connector does not crash
